questions.text: What distinguishes BERT’s masked language modeling objective from standard causal next-token prediction?

options.A: It predicts selected original tokens using context from both sides.
options.B: It predicts every next token using only the preceding token context.
options.C: It reconstructs sentence order without predicting any token identities.
options.D: It predicts selected original tokens using only the following tokens.

questions.explanation: BERT predicts original tokens at selected positions with bidirectional context, whereas causal next-token prediction conditions on preceding tokens.

questions.text: Under original BERT’s 15% selection rate and 80/10/10 corruption rule, approximately how many of 1,000 eligible tokens are replaced with [MASK]?
questions.explanation: About 150 tokens are selected, and 80% of those (120) are replaced with [MASK].

questions.text:
A token with original ID 7 is selected for MLM prediction. The corruption draw r is 0.95. What are input_ids[i] and labels[i] after this code?

```python
labels[i] = t
r = 0.95
if r < 0.8:
    input_ids[i] = MASK_ID
elif r < 0.9:
    input_ids[i] = rng.randrange(vocab_size)
# input_ids initially contains the original tokens
```
questions.explanation: The selected token retains its original label. Neither replacement branch runs at r=0.95, so the input remains 7 and still contributes to the prediction loss.
